question: Hindustani singer Pandit Venkatesh Kumar was honoured with 'Kalidas Samman-2022' by which state government?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Madhya Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Pandit Venkatesh Kumar is an eminent Hindustani classical singer known for his deep and soulful renditions.
 
• He is particularly renowned for his expertise in the Khayal form of singing.
 
• The Kalidas Samman is a prestigious arts award presented annually by the Madhya Pradesh government.
 
• It is awarded to individuals for their outstanding achievements in the fields of classical music, classical dance, theatre, and visual arts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kalidas Samman**

 
 
• Named after the celebrated classical Sanskrit writer Kalidasa, the Kalidas Samman is one of the most respected arts awards in India.
 
• It has been awarded annually since 1980 by the government of Madhya Pradesh.
 
• The award carries a plaque and a cash prize, which varies from time to time.
 
• Recipients of the Kalidas Samman have included some of the most distinguished artists, musicians, and performers in India.
 
 
 
• **Pandit Venkatesh Kumar**
 
 
• Pandit Venkatesh Kumar was born in 1953 in the Bellary district of Karnataka.
 
• He has a unique style of singing which blends the Kirana and Gwalior gharanas.
 
• He was trained under the tutelage of Puttaraj Gawai of the Veereshwara Punyashrama in Gadag.
 
• In addition to the Kalidas Samman, he has received numerous other accolades for his contributions to Indian classical music.
 
 
 
• **Hindustani Classical Music**
 
 
• Hindustani classical music is one of the two main forms of Indian classical music, the other being Carnatic music.
 
• It is known for its improvisational nature and its raga system, which uses a series of five or more musical notes upon which a melody is constructed.
 
• Hindustani music has its origins in the Vedic ritual chants and has evolved over the centuries to include various regional and cultural influences.
 
• It is traditionally performed in a solo format with instrumental accompaniment, often including a tabla and a harmonium or sarangi.
